what_its_for: Caplacizumab-yhdp is used to treat a rare but serious blood clotting disorder called acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (aTTP). In aTTP, tiny blood clots form throughout your body and your platelet count drops dangerously low. This medicine helps stop those clots from forming by blocking a protein that causes platelets to clump together in your blood vessels.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a powder that is mixed into a liquid and given as an injection. The first dose is given by your doctor or nurse directly into your vein (IV) before you start a treatment called plasma exchange. After that, you will give yourself a shot just under your skin (subcutaneous injection) once a day at home. Your healthcare team will teach you exactly how to prepare and inject the medicine safely before you leave the hospital. Always inject in your belly area, thighs, or upper arms, and rotate injection sites each time.
dosing: The usual dose is 11 mg once daily. Your very first dose is given by your healthcare team into your vein before plasma exchange begins. After that, you inject 11 mg under your skin once a day, every day, starting the morning after your first plasma exchange treatment. You continue daily injections throughout your plasma exchange treatments and then for 30 days after your last plasma exchange session. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as your condition could come back.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store the unmixed powder in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep it in its original packaging and protect it from light. Once you mix the powder with the liquid provided, use it right away and do not save it for later. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. Do not use it if the expiration date on the package has passed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other blood thinners unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as combining them with this medicine can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid activities that could cause cuts or injuries, such as contact sports, while you are on this medicine. Tell all of your doctors, dentists, and surgeons that you are taking caplacizumab-yhdp before any procedure, surgery, or dental work, because the medicine increases your bleeding risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you notice: unusual or heavy bleeding such as bleeding gums, nosebleeds that will not stop, blood in your urine or stool, coughing or vomiting blood, heavier than normal menstrual periods, cuts that will not stop bleeding, or unexplained bruising. Also contact your doctor immediately if you experience severe headache, confusion, stroke-like symptoms (sudden weakness or numbness on one side, trouble speaking or seeing), chest pain, or shortness of breath. These could be signs that your condition is getting worse or that you are having a serious complication.
when_it_works: Caplacizumab-yhdp starts working quickly, often within the first few days of treatment. Most patients see their platelet counts begin to return toward normal relatively fast compared to plasma exchange alone. However, every person is different, and your doctor will monitor your blood counts regularly to check how well the medicine is working for you. It is important to complete the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): This medicine can be used in older adults, but they may have a slightly higher risk of bleeding. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding so you can weigh the risks and benefits together. Children: The safety and effectiveness of this medicine in children under 18 years of age has not been fully established.
